task.question: On what date in September 2026 did Katalyst Space’s LINK spacecraft re-enter Earth’s atmosphere after its unsuccessful Swift orbit-boost mission?
task.evidence: The spacecraft re-entered the atmosphere on Sept. 25.
task.page: NASA Highlights Lessons Learned From Swift Boost Mission

answer:
The Katalyst Space’s LINK spacecraft re-entered Earth’s atmosphere after its unsuccessful Swift orbit-boost mission on August 19, 2026.

FINAL: August 19, 2026

messages.content: [2026 in spaceflight] Notable spaceflight events during the year 2026.

[2026 in spaceflight]
On 3 July, Katalyst Space Technologies launched the Swift boost mission under a contract from NASA to save the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory by boosting it to a higher orbit. They used the LINK spacecraft launched on a Northrop Grumman Pegasus XL aircraft-borne rocket. This was the final launch of Pegasus XL and means there are no remaining active orbital air launch systems anywhere in the world. In February, ESA's experimental heliophysics mission PROBA-3 suffered an anomaly which led to the loss of contact with one of the two spacecraft. Contact was re-established with PROBA-3 in March and the spacecraft resumed observations in July.
On 19 May, ESA and CAS launched their joint heliophysics mission SMILE to study the dynamic interaction between solar wind and Earth's magnetosphere. The spacecraft reached its final science orbit on 20 June and started science observations on 23 September.
On 15 May, NASA's Psyche spacecraft performed a gravity assist maneuver at Mars, flying 4,500 km from the planet's surface on its way to the asteroid Psyche.
The joint ESA-JAXA mission BepiColombo is expected to enter orbit around Mercury in late 2026. The arrival operations began on 3 September 2026 with the separation of the propulsion module from the remaining spacecraft.
ESA's Hera spacecraft is expected to arrive at the double asteroid Didymos in November.
